title: Grade 2 Math — Wed, Jun 03
description: 3D Solid Shapes — Day 3 of 5: Rolling, sliding and stacking
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which shape can roll but cannot be stacked?
questions.explanation: A sphere rolls in every direction and cannot sit still to be stacked.

questions.question: Which shape can only slide, never roll?
questions.explanation: A cube has only flat faces, so it slides but does not roll.

questions.question: A cylinder can roll when lying on its ___.
questions.explanation: Lying on its curved side, a cylinder rolls; standing on a flat face it does not.

questions.question: Which shapes are easiest to stack into a tower?
questions.explanation: Cubes have flat faces all around, so they stack neatly.

questions.question: A ball rolls because it has a ___ surface.
questions.explanation: Its curved (round) surface lets it roll.

questions.question: Which can both roll and be stacked when standing up?
questions.explanation: Standing on a flat end a cylinder stacks; on its side it rolls.

questions.question: Why does a cuboid NOT roll?
questions.explanation: Flat faces meet at edges and corners, so it slides instead of rolling.

questions.question: A cone lying on its side rolls in a ___.
questions.explanation: Because one end is wide and one is pointed, a cone rolls round in a circle.

questions.question: Which two shapes both roll?
questions.explanation: Both a sphere and a cylinder have curved surfaces that roll.

questions.question: To build a stable wall, which shape is best?
questions.explanation: Bricks (cuboids) have flat faces that stack without rolling away.

questions.question: Which shape would roll off a sloped table fastest?
questions.explanation: A sphere rolls freely in any direction, so it rolls off quickest.

questions.question: A shape that slides but does not roll has only ___ faces.
questions.explanation: Only flat faces means it slides — like a cube or cuboid.

questions.question: Which is the odd one out (does NOT roll)?
questions.explanation: A cube has no curved surface, so it is the only one that does not roll.

questions.question: Stacking tins on their flat ends works because the ends are ___.
questions.explanation: The flat round ends give a steady surface to stack on.

questions.question: Which group can ALL be stacked steadily?
questions.explanation: Cube, cuboid and an upright cylinder all have flat faces to stack on.
